correctness.rationale: Generator tests give \(\mathbb E[y\mid z]=0\), \(\mathbb E[x+z\mid y]=y\), and \(\mathbb E[h(x)]=0\). Exact differentiation gives \(L(x^2/2)=\alpha x(y-h(x))\) and \(L((\beta y^2+z^2)/2)=\beta(xy-y^2)\), hence \(\mathbb E[y^2]=\mathbb E[xh(x)]\). For \(m_0<0<m_1\), \(xh(x)\le0\) exactly on \(|x|\le r\), with zeros there only at \(-r,0,r\). If no mass lies beyond \(r\), the identity forces \(y=0\) and support invariance forces one of the three equilibria. The periodic crossing conclusion follows from positive outer excursion, continuity, and the zero stationary mean of \(h(x)\).

value.rationale: The two nonzero equilibria are the geometric centers around which the classical single-scroll and double-scroll dynamics are organized, and their voltage amplitude \(r\) is therefore a natural dynamical scale. The theorem turns that local equilibrium scale into a universal global restriction: every non-equilibrium compact recurrent statistical state must spend positive mass beyond it, and every periodic orbit must cross the corresponding amplitude boundary. For the canonical double-scroll slopes this gives the concrete exact threshold \(3/2\). The conditional laws and exact stationary defect apply to arbitrary compact invariant measures, not only to numerically selected attractors or individually constructed cycles.
